name: LearnPack Pedagogical Rubric v1
scope: Pedagogical quality of the generated content (objectives, text lessons, coherence between lessons, progression). Excludes presentation and ecosystem.

criteria.prompt: Considering the target audience, to what extent are the course objectives well formulated?
criteria.guidance: Objectives are well formulated: clear, measurable, at the appropriate cognitive level, and with increasing complexity. E.g.: observable verbs ('solve', 'classify') instead of 'understand'; the set advances from remember toward apply or analyze.
qualities: Appropriate cognitive level and aligned verb

criteria.prompt: To what extent is the lesson content aligned with its objectives?
criteria.guidance: Each lesson's content develops the objectives that correspond to it, at the same cognitive level and without extraneous material. E.g.: if the objective asks to 'apply', the lesson includes practice and not just definitions; there are no sections that serve no objective.

criteria.prompt: To what extent do the lessons apply principles of effective instruction and not just expose information?
criteria.guidance: Lessons teach effectively, not just expose information: they start from real problems, activate prior knowledge, demonstrate with examples, provide practice, and integrate what was learned. E.g.: open with a real case before theory; include examples and counterexamples.
qualities: Anchoring in authentic problems or tasks

criteria.prompt: Across the entire course, to what extent does the set of lessons form a coherent whole?
criteria.guidance: The set of lessons forms an articulated whole: logical sequence, consistent terminology, focus on few ideas with depth, and explicit links. E.g.: each lesson builds on the previous one; concepts already seen are revisited rather than juxtaposing loose topics.

criteria.prompt: Considering the target audience, to what extent does the course progress appropriately across all its lessons?
criteria.guidance: The trajectory reflects plausible learner development: it starts from prior knowledge, respects prerequisites, and advances gradually toward more sophisticated reasoning. E.g.: do not introduce a concept before its prerequisite; start at a reachable point without assuming expert level.
qualities: Starting point anchored in prior conceptions

frameworks.citation: Merrill, M. D. (2002). First Principles of Instruction. ETR&D, 50(3), 43-59.
Biggs, J. (1996). Enhancing teaching through constructive alignment. Higher Education, 32, 347-364.
Anderson & Krathwohl (2001); Krathwohl (2002), Theory Into Practice, 41(4), 212-218.
Biggs & Collis (1982). Evaluating the Quality of Learning: The SOLO Taxonomy.
Schmidt, Wang & McKnight (2005); Schmidt, Houang & Cogan (2002). Curriculum coherence.
Duschl, Maeng & Sezen (2011). Learning progressions and teaching sequences.
